Teaching

My teaching brings together plant science, agronomy, and horticulture through courses that connect biological principles with agricultural systems, field-based questions, and applied problem-solving.

California State University Monterey Bay

AGPS 415 — Advanced Irrigation & Nutrient Management

Upper division

Completely redesigned course integrating modern irrigation and nutrient management concepts with hands-on vegetable production in a hoop house. Students grow, manage, harvest, and analyze crops under different treatment regimes.

Field component: Huntington Farms, Soledad, CA

Selected guest speakers

  • Dr. Michael Cahn — UC Cooperative Extension, Monterey County
  • Enoch Kraycik — Irrigated Lands Program, Central Coast RWQCB

AGPS 350 — Research Methods for Crop & Soil Sciences

Upper division

Revised lecture and lab alignment to connect statistical methods and experimental design with real crop science problems. Students design, execute, and write up original experiments.

Field component: Driscoll's Research & Development, Watsonville, CA

Selected guest speakers

  • Dr. Miguel Garcia — Sustainable Agriculture Manager, Napa County RCD
  • Gerardo van den Hoek — Product Placement Specialist, Syngenta Vegetable Breeding

BIO 332 — Plant Physiology

Upper division

Redesigned course with updated structure and materials connecting plant physiology fundamentals to current research problems. Course enrollment has grown to 76 students — the largest in recent departmental history.

Selected guest speakers

  • Dr. Mina Momayyezi — Staff Research Scientist, UC Davis
  • Dr. Camila Medeiros — Postdoctoral Scholar, UCLA
  • Dr. Miquel Nadal — Research Scientist, INRAE, France

AGPS 209 — Principles of Viticulture

Lower/upper division

Designed and taught this course for the first time at CSUMB. Now permanently included in the AGPS catalog and contributing to the new AGPS minor.

Selected guest speakers

  • Dr. Maria del Mar Alsina — Senior Research Scientist, E&J Gallo Winery
  • Jarred Pearce — Enologist, Krissy Vineyards

AGPS 205 — Plants, Agriculture & Climate Change

Lower/upper division

Designed and taught this course for the first time at CSUMB. Now permanently included in the AGPS catalog and contributing to the new AGPS minor. Covers plant responses to drought and climate extremes in agricultural systems.

Selected guest speakers

  • Dr. Tapan Pathak — Associate Professor of CE, UC Merced
  • Dr. James Guilinguer — Assistant Professor, CSUMB
